analysis: AMD plunged 16.8%, underperforming the market by 12.4 percentage points, in a sell-off that tracked its AI compute peers but with greater severity. The stock fell 6.6 points more than the median of Nvidia (down 9.7%), Broadcom (down 10.3%), and TSMC (down 10.2%), while headlines point to a broad crash in chip stocks and AI-related names -- Nvidia losing nearly $1.4 trillion since October, Micron sinking 17%, and what one outlet called "The AI Trade Just Had Its Worst Day Since The Pandemic." The move comes just two sessions after AMD beat estimates by 7.5% but saw an abnormal decline of 5.7% around the report beyond what the market's move would explain, continuing a pattern where three of the last seven earnings beats were followed by negative abnormal reactions despite the company typically moving around 6.3% on reports. AMD reports next on February 2, 2027, in 89 days.
